parts.title: How to Clean a Beach
parts.subtitle: Oil spills such as the disaster in the Gulf of Mexico serve to remind us of the potential dangers of various commercial activities for our fragile oceanic environments.
parts.article:
How to Clean a Beach

(A) After the oil tanker Prestige spilt her cargo just off north-west Spain in November 2002, the beautiful beaches of the Galician coastline were covered by a metre-deep mixture of oil and seawater. The Prestige was only one incident in a long series of accidents involving oil tankers. But while each new incident, including that of the Prestige, brings environmental destruction and financial loss, it also improves our understanding of how to deal with oil spills. This knowledge is hard-won, as people have often learned from mistakes made in dealing with oil spills. Aggressive clean-ups have sometimes caused more damage than the oil. But such difficulties apart, a rough consensus on how to deal with the issues involved in cleaning up oil spills has begun to emerge.

(B) Oil is much less damaging at sea than on shore, so the best option is to skim the spilled oil off the surface of the water using specially equipped ships. A series of wooden booms floating on the surface of the water can also be used to protect the coastline. But the sea around the Prestige was too rough for the former, and much of the coast too exposed for booms to work, so there was little that could be done except watch the oil wash up onto the beaches.

(C) When oil arrives onshore, the question becomes how best to save affected plants and animals, while minimizing damage to the surrounding ecosystem, without running up a huge bill. In large spills, leaving nature to do the job is a bad idea. Even the oiliest shore will return to normal, but without human intervention this can take many years. In the case of the Prestige, both the volume of oil spilt and the wildlife, fishing and tourist value of the Galician coast demanded action by specialists.

(D) To decide what to do, specialists combined their own professional experience with local knowledge in an assessment process known as 'net environmental benefit analysis'. Factors taken into account include possible environmental destruction, such as damage to an oiled beach which is home to a breeding colony of seals or seabirds. Less immediate socio-economic repercussions also come into play: local people may rely on shellfish beds, for example, or an affected beach could be a tourist destination. And such practical realities as the cost incurred by a particular clean-up option and how easy it will be to implement are also assessed.

(E) Every intensive clean-up option has its drawbacks. When oil from the Exxon Valdez polluted the Alaskan shoreline in 1989, hot water applied under high pressure was used to scrub the beaches. But the parts of the shoreline that got this treatment recovered more slowly than those that did not. In Spain, this technique has so far been used only on man-made structures such as harbour walls.

(F) Other methods have been even more aggressive than this. When the Torrey Canyon ran aground off the south coast of England in March 1967, oiled beaches were treated with 10,000 tonnes of chemical sprays. These turned out to be more toxic than the oil: many seashore invertebrates died, and the nutrients in the dispersants caused an explosion of seaweed growth.

(G) In Galicia, local people wanted heavy machinery to come in and remove large quantities of oil quickly. But this has its own environmental cost. There were no tracks to the worst-affected beaches and it was feared that building them would harm the surrounding landscape. But in one of the areas affected, oil on the surface of the beaches was likely to be washed into the pipe that supplied water to a large fish farm. In the end, the desire to safeguard the farm tipped the balance in favour of building tracks for bulldozers and earthmovers, which scooped up the oil from the beach. Such equipment was not used in all areas affected by the Prestige spill, however. Salt-marshes and estuaries are such delicate terrain that almost any activity does more damage than the oil.

(H) After the Amoco Cadiz disaster in 1978, when nearly a quarter of a million tonnes of oil were spilt off the coast of north-western France, heavy equipment was sent in to some polluted salt-marshes, where it scraped up the top half-metre of sediment. Twelve years later, these areas had still not recovered, whereas the oiled marshes that went uncleaned seemed in good shape.

(I) After a short period of time, the Prestige spill moved from the emergency phase—high profile, high pressure—to a long-term painstaking project. Cleaning the beaches, for example, was a huge task. At Carnota, one of the most heavily affected areas of Galicia, dozens of volunteers and soldiers worked their way along six kilometres of sand on hands and knees, scraping up the small lumps of solidified oil. At other beaches nearby, people sifted the sand and combed seaside plants by hand to remove the oil and stop it becoming buried.

(J) Once workers there had done all they could, stubborn patches still remained on rocks and in crevices. A possibility was to move oily rocks down the beach into the surf since this accelerates the natural cleaning process, as can 'flushing'—i.e. pumping seawater over the shore and sifting the oil out of the run-off. But as the coastline became cleaner, the clean-up started to cost more for progressively less reward and more environmental damage. The Galicians were then faced with perhaps their most difficult decision: when to stop. As with most such operations, this decision is usually taken by local politicians rather than by environmentalists.

questions.question: Each new oil spill improves our understanding of how to deal with such incidents.

analyses.content: 题目提到每次漏油事故都能增进我们对处理此事的了解，原文明确说每一次新事件都提高了我们应对漏油的认知。
你可能看到前半句的“带来环境破坏和经济损失”就觉得是负面影响，但别漏了后半句明确肯定的“提高认知”。

But while each new incident, including that of the Prestige, brings environmental destruction and financial loss, it also improves our understanding of how to deal with oil spills. This knowledge is hard-won, as people have often learned from mistakes made in dealing with oil spills.

questions.question: Aggressive clean-ups have sometimes caused more damage than the oil itself.

analyses.content: 题目说激进的清理有时造成的破坏比石油本身还大，原文一模一样地指出了这一点。
你可能会因为题目里的“sometimes（有时候）”觉得不够绝对而不敢选，但原文用的恰好也是这个词，完美对应。
Aggressive clean-ups have sometimes caused more damage than the oil.

questions.question: The Prestige disaster caused more damage than any previous oil spill in the region.

analyses.content: 原文只说了“威望号”是众多油轮事故中的一次，完全没有拿它的破坏程度去和该地区的其他事故做比较。
你可能会根据常识或者第一句描写的严重程度自己脑补它是最惨烈的，但只要文章没明确比较，就只能选“未提及”。
The Prestige was only one incident in a long series of accidents involving oil tankers.

questions.question: It is best to let nature clean up large oil spills without any human intervention.

analyses.content: 题目说大型漏油事件最好顺其自然不加干预，而原文直接反驳说这完全是个“糟糕的主意”。
你可能看到下一句写着“最终都会恢复正常”就觉得不干预也行，但原文紧接着强调了不人为干预的话需要耗费很多年。
In large spills, leaving nature to do the job is a bad idea. Even the oiliest shore will return to normal, but without human intervention this can take many years.

questions.question: Most oil spills are caused by poor maintenance of tankers.

analyses.content: 原文确实提到了油轮事故频发，但从头到尾都没解释这些事故是不是因为“维护不善（poor maintenance）”造成的。
你可能凭常识觉得漏油就是船没保养好，但做阅读题绝不能带入个人常识，没写原因就是未提及。
The Prestige was only one incident in a long series of accidents involving oil tankers.

Deciding how to respond to an oil spill
When specialists have to decide how to react to an oil spill, they use a process called ‘net environmental benefit analysis’. In this process, they combine their professional experience with . They consider the possible environmental destruction, as well as less immediate effects on the local community. Practical issues, including the of each option, are assessed too.
Every intensive clean-up method has disadvantages. Following the Exxon Valdez spill, under high pressure was used on the beaches, but this slowed their recovery. After the Torrey Canyon ran aground, the beaches were treated with , which proved to be more toxic than the oil itself.

analyses.content: 题目问专家把专业经验和什么结合了起来，原文明确指出是将专业经验与“当地知识（local knowledge）”相结合。
你找答案时要紧盯“combined with”这个动作对应的词，别被后面那串长长的专有名词（评估过程）带偏了方向。
To decide what to do, specialists combined their own professional experience with local knowledge in an assessment process known as 'net environmental benefit analysis'.
题目缺一个形容词来修饰对当地社区“不那么直接的影响”，原文直接给出了“不那么直接的社会经济（socio-economic）影响”。
你可能想填后面的名词“repercussions（影响）”，但题干空格前面缺的是一个修饰性质的词，必须填“socio-economic”。
Less immediate socio-economic repercussions also come into play: local people may rely on shellfish beds, for example, or an affected beach could be a tourist destination.
题目问评估方案时包括了哪些实际问题，原文列举的实际情况里，第一个提到的就是特定方案产生的“成本（cost）”。
你可能会被同一句里的“how easy”吸引，但这里需要填一个名词，“cost”是最直接且符合字数要求的目标词。
And such practical realities as the cost incurred by a particular clean-up option and how easy it will be to implement are also assessed.
题目问在阿拉斯加漏油事件中，海滩上高压使用了什么导致恢复减慢，原文明确说是高压喷射的“热水（hot water）”。
你可能想把动词“applied”也填上去，但它是用来修饰的，这里的核心物品只有“hot water”。

When oil from the Exxon Valdez polluted the Alaskan shoreline in 1989, hot water applied under high pressure was used to scrub the beaches. But the parts of the shoreline that got this treatment recovered more slowly than those that did not.
题目问托雷峡谷号事件中，海滩被什么比油还毒的物质处理了，原文点明喷洒了一万吨的“化学喷雾（chemical sprays）”，并补充它比油毒。
你可能一眼扫过去想填前面的数字“10,000 tonnes”，但这只是数量，题干问的是产生毒性的核心物质。

When the Torrey Canyon ran aground off the south coast of England in March 1967, oiled beaches were treated with 10,000 tonnes of chemical sprays. These turned out to be more toxic than the oil: many seashore invertebrates died, and the nutrients in the dispersants caused an explosion of seaweed growth.

questions.question: What did the Amoco Cadiz disaster demonstrate about salt-marshes?

analyses.content: 题目问阿莫科·卡迪兹灾难证明了盐沼的什么特性，原文说被重型设备清理过的盐沼12年都没恢复，没清理的反而状态挺好，说明不清理更好。
你可能会凭直觉选C认为机器清理最有效，但这完全无视了原文所说的“机械清理导致环境长达12年无法恢复”的惨痛教训。

After the Amoco Cadiz disaster in 1978, when nearly a quarter of a million tonnes of oil were spilt off the coast of north-western France, heavy equipment was sent in to some polluted salt-marshes, where it scraped up the top half-metre of sediment. Twelve years later, these areas had still not recovered, whereas the oiled marshes that went uncleaned seemed in good shape.

questions.question: How was the oil mainly removed from the beaches at Carnota?

analyses.content: 题目问在Carnota海滩上主要是怎么除油的，原文描述人们是“手脚并用（on hands and knees）”爬行着把油刮起来的，也就是完全靠手工清理。
你可能看到下一句提到了“筛沙子（sifted the sand）”就犹豫其他选项，但题目明确问的是Carnota这个地方的做法，对应句子里的核心动作就是手和膝盖。

At Carnota, one of the most heavily affected areas of Galicia, dozens of volunteers and soldiers worked their way along six kilometres of sand on hands and knees, scraping up the small lumps of solidified oil.

questions.question: According to the writer, who usually decides when to stop a clean-up operation?

analyses.content: 题目问谁来决定什么时候停止清理，原文最后一句清晰地点明，这种决定通常是由“当地政客（local politicians）”做出的。
你可能理所当然地认为专业的事情肯定是A（环保专家）负责，但作者特意写了“而不是环保人士（rather than by environmentalists）”来直接排除这个选项。

The Galicians were then faced with perhaps their most difficult decision: when to stop. As with most such operations, this decision is usually taken by local politicians rather than by environmentalists.
